quality.description: The core R-SIM-11 regression is never run by an automated gate. Only the synthetic-data unit test `roll-return-checks.test.mjs` and the Python adapter tests are added to `test`. `roll-return-native.mjs` is registered only as the opt-in script `test:roll-return`, and `disturbance-input.browser.mjs` only as `test:roll-return-browser`. Neither is chained into `test:browser`, while many comparable native and browser regressions are. A future adapter, model or bridge change could reintroduce retained aileron history without any CI or browser-suite failure. Expected: chain `node ../studies/e1-browser/sim/roll-return-native.mjs` into `test:browser` (or an equivalent gated suite), and preferably the browser harness too. Reproduction: inspect the `test:browser` chain; neither roll-return entry point appears in it.
quality.evidence: packet sources app/package.json `test:browser` value; source_diff adds only `test:roll-return` and `test:roll-return-browser`; ci.summary lists 555 Node tests with no native roll-return wrapper output.

quality.description: The admission function hard-fails unless every sampled post-release roll rate (from 1 s on) is below the release-instant rate (`initialRate > 0 && laterRate < initialRate`). That is an aircraft-dynamics assertion inside a contract that explicitly is not a prescribed self-leveling rate. A legitimate future aerodynamic or loading change could fail the control-return regression even though surfaces still return exactly. Expected: report the guard as a diagnostic or keep it in a separately named check, so the surface-return identity is not coupled to dynamic response.
quality.evidence: packet roll-return-checks.mjs lines computing initialRate/laterRate and the assert; criterion text 'not a prescribed self-leveling rate'.

quality.location: app/tests/disturbance-input.browser.mjs (pointer-right-15px camera block and case push)
quality.description: Maintainability: `record.camera` is assigned twice; the first assignment, which includes `final_state`, is immediately overwritten after the asserts. `if(!result.cases.includes(record))result.cases.push(record)` is dead code because the record was already pushed. `const lon=s?...final_state[2]:0` guards on `s` while `lat` is read unguarded on the same stats object. The behaviour is correct, but the redundancy obscures which fields are artifact contract.
quality.evidence: packet disturbance-input.browser.mjs camera block and the line following it.

quality.description: On failure the catch block runs `result.after=await hashes()` before `throw e`. If `hashes()` itself rejects (missing file, unreadable root), the original assertion error is replaced and lost from both the process exit and the artifact. Expected: wrap the post-failure hashing in its own try/catch, record any secondary error in `result.errors`, and rethrow the original `e`.

In installed (no-override) mode the harness pins only `dist/jsbsim.wasm`, not `dist/jsbsim.mjs` or `dist/build-info.json`. The installed-ROOT artifact therefore records no glue or metadata identity (`variant: unchanged ROOT`), so the prepared-model identity of the actual-app run is inferred from the WASM hash alone. Expected: add the glue and build-info paths to the before/after source hashes.
quality.evidence: packet `paths` constant; browsers.new_installed.variant and before/after maps.

validation.criterion: R-SIM-11: remove only the two source aileron actuator hysteresis bands in the generic prepared manual-control model
validation.expected: Only the `hysteresis_width` of `fcs/left-aileron-actuator` and `fcs/right-aileron-actuator` changes, 0.005 to 0, with fail-closed handling of unknown, partial or duplicate wiring.
validation.observed: The source code establishes the narrow change. `patch_aileron_hysteresis` replaces exactly one line-exact width inside each uniquely named actuator block and rejects missing, duplicate, nested, unclosed, renamed, unknown-value and partial-pair cases. Production is gated by the pinned source SHA, and the patch is idempotent. Adapter tests cover these branches. The preservation record says exactly two values changed (prepared model 02d1811a→cd85bb2a), and the AP XML is unchanged (5e97d48b).
validation.evidence: sources prepare-aircraft.py; prepare-aircraft.test.py (missing/unknown/duplicate/partial/unclosed cases); preservation.only_two_values_changed; old_build/new_build aircraft_adapter hashes.

validation.criterion: R-SIM-11: preserve source aileron rate limits/scales, trim handoff, pilot gain, mass, pitch/yaw channels and aerodynamic functions byte-for-byte
validation.expected: Every byte other than the two width values is identical; bridge, loading and aerodynamics are unchanged; initial trim is identical.
validation.observed: The transform is a single in-place byte replacement per actuator, and the other v4 patches are unchanged, so the remaining bytes are preserved by construction. Hashes are unchanged for the bridge (e7164692), `loading.js` (b36361f5), the AP XML, the engine/propeller and the native library (85bbfda4); `aerodynamics_equal` is true. Native neutral fixtures produce identical digests old vs new (for example 60-neutral 187d5adb098bf633), and initial surface angles and roll are identical. Browser `roll_trim_norm`/`yaw_trim_norm` and initial surface angles are identical. Native `balance()` identity is asserted unchanged through every run.
validation.evidence: prepare-aircraft.py; preservation (aerodynamics_equal, bridge_equal, build hashes); native_old vs native_new neutral digests and initial rows; test_only_named_roll_actuators_have_zero_width_while_other_source_bytes_stay.

validation.criterion: R-SIM-11: signed pulse/release fixtures return the same command/trim to the same actual surface position (native)
validation.expected: For ±0.02/±0.05/±0.1 aileron pulses at 60/80/100 kt, both actual surfaces return to their own pre-pulse positions after the rate-limit delay, within the 1e-10 degree numerical budget.
validation.observed: All 18 signed cases report `max_returned_surface_residual_deg` of 0. Raw native_new release rows at +0.5..20 s equal the initial left/right values exactly (for example 60-aileron--0.1: -0.1963465685635314 / 0.14725992642264854). The strict admission checker requires complete ordered samples, unique identities, finite telemetry and raw-derived deltas, and compares each returned surface to its own initial value.
validation.evidence: regression.cases; native_new cases release arrays; roll-return-checks.mjs; roll-return-checks.test.mjs.

validation.criterion: R-SIM-11: same returned position regardless of prior pulse (history independence)
validation.expected: Successive opposite pulses within one flight leave no retained surface history.
validation.observed: There are 54 within-flight checks: six alternating pulses (±0.1, ±0.05, ±0.02) at each of three CAS values, sampled at 0.5/1/2 s after release, all measured against the pre-first-pulse surface positions. Every `surface_residual_rad` is 0, and commands are asserted to be zero.

validation.expected: Post-release native roll-rate and bank observations are recorded against a matched neutral run.
validation.observed: The native diagnostic records p, bank, beta and surface data at seven integer-aligned release samples, with delta_vs_neutral, for all 57 cases. The regression reports release and later roll rates. For example, at 80 kt +0.02, the 20 s bank delta is +0.476° new vs +8.46° old. The criterion prescribes no rate tolerance, and none is claimed.

validation.criterion: R-SIM-11 / R-INPUT-1: actual-app observations of the returned command/trim reaching the same surface position
validation.expected: In the actual installed app, pointer and keyboard pulses of both signs release all axes to zero, and both finite actual surfaces return to their own initial trimmed angles.
validation.observed: The installed five-case run, with no native override, executed the exact expected IDs with `suite.complete` true and result/return status pass. The four signed pointer/keyboard rows pass 24 paired return checks with zero residual at +0.5..20 s; the neutral row is correctly `not_evaluated`. Released axes are zero, AP is off and the simulation rate is 1×. ROOT hashes match before and after (wasm 266f2016). The harness hash e3e44f81 matches the manifest. Neutral-only reports not_evaluated and the subset reports partial.

quality.description: The supplement chains only the native roll-return regression into `test:browser`. The actual-app browser harness `tests/disturbance-input.browser.mjs` is still opt-in through `test:roll-return-browser`. The prior medium finding asked for the native script and said 'preferably the browser harness too'. As it stands, a regression in the UI input path (pointer or keyboard release not reaching zero, or a bridge or worker change) that does not show up natively would not fail the normal browser gate.
